description: Anthracnose is a fungal disease causing circular, sunken, dark lesions on succulent leaves, often progressing under moist and humid conditions.
symptoms: Sunken, water-soaked round or oval dark lesions on leaf surfaces
Lesions may expand and merge, causing leaf tissue to become soft or necrotic
Older lesions may develop dark concentric rings or spore masses under persistent moisture

sanitation.step: Carefully remove and dispose of badly affected leaves to eliminate primary inoculum sources.
sources: General Plant Pathology Principles (Agrios, Plant Pathology 5th Ed)

sanitation.step: Sterilize shears or knives with rubbing alcohol or a mild bleach solution between prunings.

cultural.step: Ensure high air circulation around plants and keep humidity levels moderate in growing spaces.
Water exclusively from below at the container base; avoid spraying or splashing water onto foliage.

precautions.step: Do not compost diseased tissue in household compost bins where fungal spores can survive.
